We had many people in our comments who assumed we were just random people who bought a tiger cub and many people asking where they can get a tiger. We want to address this because it’s very important. Rick is not just a normal person with a tiger. Rick owns a USDA licensed zoo and Mowgli is not a personal pet. Mowgli came from another zoo and was not purchased as a pet. The reason Mowgli is inside the house (which is on the zoo property) is because he is not fully vaccinated and we will not allow him outside until our vet clears us for that. Anyone who is wanting a pet tiger needs to know that you cannot legally own one as a pet. Also, this is not Rick’s first Tiger. You can go and see Kai, our female, on our page. Rick has extensive experience with big cats and raising them. You can however enjoy how cute he is on our social media! We will NEVER have tiger encounters available and no visitors will ever be allowed to touch him or interact with him. When he is older and cleared to go outside you can see him in his enclosure if you visit the zoo. We hope that clears a few things up!

Any comments calling this out as unethical are swarmed by people saying “this is a wildlife park they know what they’re doing”. People don’t realize that these “wildlife parks” are started up so that people can get the permits to legally own these exotics as pets, and they’ll often use them for profit to have access to more exotics. It’s not a zoo, it’s one persons desire to own tigers and lions and bears as pets and treat them as such, and the messages it sends are incredibly dangerous. Not only that, but NO ethical zoo would ever sell a tiger this young to another zoo, and no ethical zoo would buy a tiger this young from another zoo.  TWP is an unethical facility doing and promoting dangerous things with animals and unfortunately these types of places get a lot of support because the general public wants to play with animals and see cute animal content. When Kallie was rescued by Lions Tigers & Bears, she had been abandoned and left to die. Her condition was so critical that she required extensive emergency medical care, multiple surgeries, and ultimately a life-saving leg amputation. Against all odds, Kallie never gave up. Today, Kallie is thriving on three legs, living the life she always deserved at Lions Tigers & Bears. She continues to receive specialized daily care from our dedicated team, and every step she takes is a reminder of what’s possible when compassion meets action. Your support made Kallie’s second chance possible. Thank you for standing with us as we rescue, rehabilitate, and provide lifelong sanctuary to animals who have nowhere else to turn.
